text.p: The lira ended 1996 sharply lower while Treasury bill and bond yields continued to slide on news of a sharp rise in witholding tax on government securities in 1997. The lira closed at 108,290 per dollar, down from 108,020 on Monday, as a cash surplus prompted traders to sell the currency for dollars in the last trading day of 1996.

The Turkish central bank drained 38.2 trillion lira of excess cash through overnight money at 57 percent while lending banks 22.7 trillion lira through tomorrow/next at 74 percent and 2.3 trillion via tomorrow/week deals at 75 percent.
The market opened with 26 trillion lira excess cash in the morning, dealers said.

Treasury bill and bond yields fell by another three to six points after Monday's six point plunge. Demand for outstanding paper had surged on a Friday announcement that witholding tax would be raised to 12 pct from the current 10 on interest income from government paper to be issued in 1997.
The total fall in T-bill and bond yields reached 16 points in some maturities since Friday.
The average yield on the most active June 4, 1997 paper plunged 10 percent to 95.10 percent from 105.21 at the Monday close. The total fall since Friday was 15.7 points.

The second-most active paper yield -- maturing October 30, 1997 -- fell to 102.16 percent, down from Monday's 106.16 percent and Friday's 112.46 percent. -- Tulin Aygunes, Istanbul newsroom +90-212-275 08 75 ATA
